title: The impact of AI-supported online classroom management (AIS-OCM) on attitudes toward english lessons, self-directed online learning, and academic achievement
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-supported online classroom management (AIS-OCM) can improve middle school students’ attitudes toward English as a Foreign Language (EFL), their self-directed online learning skills, and their academic achievement. The authors argue that online learning often suffers from reduced interaction, weaker motivation, and limited feedback, especially in language learning contexts that require frequent communication and timely correction.

To address this problem, the study implemented AIS-OCM in a seventh-grade EFL setting using the Zoom platform and the AI-supported language learning tool Rosetta Stone. The intervention combined adaptive content, automated speech-recognition feedback, individualized practice, automated monitoring, and teacher use of AI-generated dashboards and reports. A control group received the same online instruction without AI integration. The study used a pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design over eight weeks with two seventh-grade classes from the same school in Turkey.

Results from mixed ANOVA showed that both groups improved over time, but the AIS-OCM group generally performed better. The strongest and most consistent benefits appeared for self-directed online learning and academic achievement, while attitude gains were positive but sometimes not significantly different in growth rate between groups. Overall, the paper concludes that AI-supported online classroom management can meaningfully enhance online EFL instruction by supporting learner autonomy, improving feedback and monitoring, and contributing to better academic outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control-group study with baseline comparisons, standardized instruction, and a comparison group, but it lacks random assignment and is limited to one school and small sample sizes. Internal validity is reasonably supported, though not at the level of a well-controlled RCT.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports modest-to-moderate positive effects, with several outcomes showing partial η2 values around or above 0.06 and one achievement interaction effect at ηp2=0.062. Impacts are meaningful for a priority middle-school EFL population, but generalizability is limited by the quasi-experimental single-site design.

interventions.use_case: AI-supported EFL instruction using Rosetta Stone with speech recognition, automated pronunciation feedback, personalized language practice, and adaptive content during synchronous online classroom management
Adaptive learning pathways and personalized time-management/learning recommendations based on student performance analytics within the AIS-OCM setup
Teacher dashboards and automated monitoring reports used to track participation, progress, and learning difficulties during online English lessons

finding.finding_summary: The intervention improved English-language performance in a middle-school EFL context over an 8-week quasi-experiment (n=65; 32 experimental, 33 control). Academic achievement scores rose significantly over time in both groups, with a significant group difference and Time×Group interaction for Unit 2 (F(1,63)=4.14, p=0.046, ηp2=0.062), indicating greater gains for the AI-supported group.
finding.measure: English academic achievement tests for Unit 1 (Appearance and Personality) and Unit 2 (Sports)
finding.effect_size: ηp2=0.062 (Unit 2 Time×Group); ηp2=0.941 and 0.957 for time main effects

finding.finding_summary: AIS-OCM improved students’ attitudes toward English lessons, with significant main effects of time and group for both affective and behavioral subdimensions. For example, affective attitudes showed F(1,63)=11.29, p=0.001, ηp2=0.152 and behavioral attitudes showed F(1,63)=16.41, p<0.001, ηp2=0.207, suggesting moderate improvements across the 8-week intervention (n=65).
finding.measure: Attitudes toward English Lessons Scale (ATELS), affective and behavioral subdimensions

finding.finding_summary: The AI-supported condition improved self-directed online learning, especially autonomous learning. The autonomous learning subscale showed a significant Time×Group interaction (F(1,63)=4.20, p=0.045, ηp2=0.063), and both self-directed learning subdimensions favored the experimental group overall (n=65).
finding.measure: Self-Directed Online Learning Scale (SDOLS), autonomous learning and asynchronous online learning subdimensions
finding.effect_size: ηp2=0.063 (autonomous Time×Group); ηp2=0.198 (group main effect, autonomous)
